title: Requirements, User Stories and Project Scope
learningObjectives: Explain the purpose and value of Requirements, User Stories and Project Scope.
Apply requirements, user stories and project scope to a Python project scenario.
Identify decisions and trade-offs relevant to requirements, user stories and project scope.
Review common mistakes and risks in requirements, user stories and project scope.
Produce a verifiable project artifact using requirements, user stories and project scope principles.

understand.concept: Requirements describe system behaviour and quality constraints. Functional requirements specify capabilities; non-functional requirements cover usability, reliability, performance, privacy and accessibility. User stories express a need from a user's perspective.
understand.whyItMatters: Clear requirements make implementation and acceptance decisions less subjective.
understand.analogy: A travel plan describes the destination and constraints before choosing the route.
understand.analogyLimit: User stories are prompts for discussion, not complete specifications.
understand.summary: Requirements, User Stories and Project Scope helps learners plan and deliver maintainable Python projects.

explain.narrative: Write observable functional requirements and relevant quality constraints. A user story follows As a [user], I want [capability], so that [benefit]. Prioritize requirements and keep non-goals visible to control scope.

examples.title: Quality requirement
examples.explanation: Response time is a quality constraint.

examples.title: User story
examples.code:
story = 'As a teacher, I want to record marks so that I can prepare reports.'
print(story.startswith('As a teacher'))
examples.explanation: A story frames capability and benefit.

practise.guidedTask: Write functional and non-functional requirements for a student marks application.
practise.independentTask: Rewrite a vague request as measurable requirements.
hints: Use observable verbs such as create, search, export and reject.
State measurable limits when performance matters.
practise.challenge: Create prioritized requirements for a library lending application.
validationCriteria: The project concept is accurately explained and applied.
All examples execute with documented output on Python 3.13.
The proposed artifact is testable and appropriate to stated requirements.
Trade-offs, limitations and relevant risks are acknowledged.
